title: Harmony, Voice Leading, and Rhythm
description: Triads to function, voice leading as a craft, then chromaticism and mixture — the bridge from common-practice grammar toward the vocabulary heavy music actually uses.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 21M.301 Harmony and Counterpoint I
sourceReferences.notes: Species counterpoint and four-part writing as the way harmonic function becomes a craft. Voice leading is a prerequisite to analysis.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 21M.302 Harmony and Counterpoint II
sourceReferences.notes: Chromaticism, mixture, modulation. The bridge toward the chromatic vocabulary heavy music uses.

modules.title: Harmonic function
learningObjectives: Spell a triad or seventh and name its function in a key
Write a short progression that cadences instead of just listing chords

modules.title: Voice leading
learningObjectives: Move voices by step where you can, and name the dissonance when you cannot
Hold a pedal or drop a voice without losing the part

modules.title: Chromaticism
learningObjectives: Borrow, tonicize, or leave the key on purpose
Give an outside pitch a job instead of calling it color

concepts.name: Triads
concepts.summary: Three notes stacked in thirds.
objectives: Spell a triad as root, third, and fifth from a scale degree
Hear major, minor, diminished, and augmented as four qualities

concepts.name: Seventh chords
concepts.summary: A fourth note, and a new set of tendencies.
objectives: Add a seventh to a triad and name the quality
Predict the tendency of a chordal seventh in common-practice writing

concepts.name: Inversion
concepts.summary: The same pitch classes, a different bass.
objectives: Put a chord tone other than the root in the bass
Read a figured bass or a slash as an inversion, not a new chord

concepts.name: Tonic, predominant, dominant
concepts.summary: Three jobs a chord can have in a key.
objectives: Assign tonic, predominant, or dominant function in a key
Predict which function a ii or a V is doing in a short progression

concepts.name: Cadences
concepts.summary: How a phrase decides it is over.
objectives: End a phrase with a cadence you can name
Distinguish authentic, half, plagal, and deceptive by what they leave open

concepts.name: Common-practice progression
concepts.summary: A grammar, not a law of nature.
objectives: Write a short common-practice progression that prepares and resolves
Predict a weak move if two functions are skipped or repeated without reason

concepts.name: Phrase and period
concepts.summary: Antecedent and consequent as a small form.
objectives: Group bars into a phrase that breathes, and a period that answers
Mark a phrase ending that is not yet a section ending

concepts.name: Fifths without a third
concepts.summary: A dyad that refuses to be major or minor.
objectives: Play a fifth without a third and treat it as a harmonic object
Predict what distortion does to that fifth's partials

concepts.name: Voice leading
concepts.summary: Each part as a line, not a stack of names.
objectives: Move each voice by the smallest honest step
Rewrite a leap that could have been a common tone

concepts.name: Species counterpoint as a craft
concepts.summary: Constraints that teach you what a line can do.
objectives: Use species counterpoint as a craft that teaches what a line can do
Write a first-species pair that keeps independence

concepts.name: Parallel fifths and octaves
concepts.summary: Why they were banned, and when a riff does not care.
objectives: State why parallel fifths and octaves were banned in that craft
Decide when a riff does not owe that ban anything

concepts.name: Tendency tones
concepts.summary: Leading tones and chordal sevenths that want to resolve.
objectives: Name a leading tone or chordal seventh as a pitch that wants a resolution
Resolve one on purpose and leave one hanging on purpose

concepts.name: Dissonance as a timed event
concepts.summary: A clash that is prepared, struck, and left.
objectives: Treat a clash as a timed event: prepared, struck, left
Write a suspension that is not just a wrong note

concepts.name: Non-chord tones
concepts.summary: Passing, neighbor, suspension — names for how you got there.
objectives: Name passing, neighbor, and suspension as ways you arrived
Label a non-chord tone instead of respelling the harmony

concepts.name: Texture
concepts.summary: How many parts, and whether they share a rhythm.
objectives: Count the parts and say whether they share a rhythm
Contrast unison, homophony, and independent lines in a short excerpt

concepts.name: Drop voicings
concepts.summary: Spreading a close position by dropping a voice an octave.
objectives: Drop a voice an octave to spread a close position
Write a drop-2 voicing from a close triad

concepts.name: Pedal point
concepts.summary: A held bass against changing harmony.
objectives: Hold a bass against changing harmony
Predict the clash a pedal is supposed to create and then release

concepts.name: Secondary dominants
concepts.summary: Temporarily treating another chord as a tonic.
objectives: Temporarily treat another chord as a tonic with its own dominant
Write a V/V that actually tonicizes, not a random major chord

concepts.name: Modal mixture
concepts.summary: Borrowing a chord from the parallel mode.
objectives: Borrow a chord from the parallel mode
Predict the color of a bVI or a minor iv in a major key

concepts.name: Modulation
concepts.summary: Changing tonic and meaning it.
objectives: Change tonic and mean it, with a pivot or a direct shift
Distinguish a tonicization that comes home from a modulation that stays

concepts.name: Chromaticism
concepts.summary: Pitches outside the key that still have a job.
objectives: Give an outside pitch a job: approach, color, or new tonic
Rewrite a chromatic line that is only filling space

concepts.name: Neapolitan and augmented sixths
concepts.summary: Predominants that approach the dominant from the side.
objectives: Approach the dominant from a lowered second or an augmented sixth
Spell a Neapolitan or It+6 so the resolution is honest

concepts.name: Sequence
concepts.summary: A pattern that transposes itself.
objectives: Transpose a pattern so the sequence is the form
Predict where a sequence must break to cadence
